newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cenbank may hang on to Rio's Banerj for now.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cenbank may hang on to Rio's Banerj for now.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank may extend its special administration of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banco Banerj SA, which expires on June 26, to avoid the bank's liquidation, said a Central Bank spokesman.

The extension would give Rio state more time to privatize the bank as the Banerj auction still hinges on a Senate approval of a 3.09 billion real loan by federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF).
The loan would be used to clear up Banerj's pension and payroll-related debt and make the bank more appealing to private investors.
If Banerj is not privatized by June 26 and an extension is not approved, the bank would have to be liquidated.
The spokesman said the Central Bank may extend its special administration for at least another 45 days. He noted, however, that the bank has not made any decision yet.
Banerj has been under Central Bank administration since December 1994. But it has been managed day-to-day by private bank Banco Bozano, Simonsen since January last year on behalf of the Central Bank.
Bozano was hired to ready the bank for privatization.
The Banerj auction, originally scheduled for June 17, remains on hold pending the Senate approval of the loan.
Four private banks -- Bradesco, Banco Itau, BCN, and Cia de Investimentos Latino-Americana, owned by a foreign bank and represented by local Banco Pactual -- have signed up for the Banerj auction.
The state hoped to offer the bank to investors today, but the sale could not take place because a Senate committee delayed until next week an expected vote on the Banerj deal.
The deal must be first pass the Senate panel before it is put to a vote on the floor of the upper house.
